title: FCC green-lights 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites
subtitle: Direct-to-device, 150 Mbps targets, and a path to compete with the big three carriers.
title_narration: F C C green-lights 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites.
as_of: Grounded in Jim's Interest Journal research for Wed Oct 7, 2026. The FCC grant was Tue Oct 6 and reported Wed.

scenes.label: The grant
scenes.heading: Next-gen Starlink Mobile, approved
scenes.caption: The FCC approved 15,000 next-gen Starlink Mobile direct-to-device satellites. The grant was Tuesday October 6 and was reported Wednesday.
evidence: FCC approved 15,000 next-gen Starlink Mobile (direct-to-device) satellites.
The grant was Tue Oct 6 and was reported Wed.

scenes.label: Spectrum
scenes.heading: What SpaceX can use

cards.label: spectrum in the acquisition — testing only until close (11/30/2027)

scenes.caption: SpaceX can use the EchoStar spectrum it's acquiring, for testing only until that deal closes on November 30, 2027, and T-Mobile's PCS G-block.
evidence: SpaceX can use the EchoStar spectrum it's acquiring (testing only until that deal closes, scheduled 11/30/2027) and T-Mobile's PCS G-block.
scenes.narration: SpaceX can use the EchoStar spectrum it's acquiring, for testing only until that deal closes on November 30, 2027, and T-Mobile's P C S G-block.

scenes.label: The waiver
scenes.heading: No terrestrial carrier partner required

lines: Opens a path to compete with *AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon*.

scenes.caption: The FCC waived the requirement that SpaceX partner with a terrestrial carrier. That opens a path for Starlink Mobile to compete directly with AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon.
evidence: The FCC waived the requirement that SpaceX partner with a terrestrial carrier. That opens a path for Starlink Mobile to compete directly with AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon.

scenes.label: Speed promise
scenes.heading: From today's D2D to 5G-like targets
scenes.caption: SpaceX is promising about 150 megabits per user, 5G-like, versus about 4 megabits today on roughly 650 satellites.
evidence: SpaceX is promising about 150 Mbps per user (5G-like), versus about 4 Mbps today on roughly 650 sats.
scenes.narration: SpaceX is promising about 150 megabits per user, 5G-like, versus about 4 megabits today on roughly 650 satellites.

scenes.label: Deadlines
scenes.heading: When the constellation must fly

events.label: FCC grant for 15,000 Starlink Mobile sats

scenes.caption: Deadlines: 50 percent launched by October 2032 and the full constellation by October 2035. On Wednesday the FCC also proposed opening more spectrum for direct-to-device service.
evidence: Deadlines: 50% launched by Oct 2032 and the full constellation by Oct 2035.
